question.text: In a bonus issue with a ratio of 1:2, what does a shareholder holding 500 shares receive?

explanation.text: The Logic: A 1:2 bonus means 1 bonus share for every 2 shares held. For 500 shares held, bonus shares = 500 / 2 = 250. The Trap: Candidates may misread 1:2 as 2 bonus shares for every 1 held. Read bonus ratios as "new shares : existing shares" — 1:2 means 1 new for every 2 existing. Note: Apply the bonus ratio as a simple proportion of the existing holding to obtain the number of bonus shares.
